issues.description: Exercise 1's simulate() method in the template is annotated to return list[complex], while the problem statement and the solution expect/produce a Qiskit statevector (Statevector object or numpy.ndarray). This mismatch between the annotated return type in the template and the actual/expected returned type (statevector) can confuse students about the expected return value and its format.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's simulate() return type consistent with the problem statement and solution. Either change the template type hint to reflect the Qiskit statevector type (e.g., return Statevector or numpy.ndarray) or modify the solution to convert the statevector to a list[complex] before returning. Update the docstring to state precisely which type/format (Statevector, numpy array, or list of complex) students should return.

issues.description: The template implementation of the Lights Out puzzle uses the parameter name 'switch_register' in the state_preparation() signature, while the problem statement and the solution use the term 'flip_register'. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual query register (the register representing which switches/flips to apply) can confuse students mapping the exercise description to the template stub and to the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the 'switch_register' parameter in the template state_preparation() signature (and any internal uses) to 'flip_register' so it matches the problem statement terminology and the solution implementation. Alternatively, update all references to use a single consistent name (flip_register) across template, problem text, and solution.
